//: STAMPED from the source of truth for the answer-key deny-guards (D30). This template lives on the secret side; the repo's .claude/settings.json is stamped from it. Edit HERE and re-stamp; never hand-edit the repo copy. The guards cover the secret TIER (the held-out answer key, invoice index, generators, discrepancy-design artifact) and DELIBERATELY NOT the held-out inputs directory (goldset-triad-holdout), which the agent must read to produce findings (D14). Placement outside the repo tree is the primary control; these rules are the second layer. NOTE the answer-key filename rule is deliberately UNSCOPED ('**/holdout_answer_key.json', not '**/goldset-triad-secret/**/holdout_answer_key.json'): scoped to the secret directory it would merely restate the directory rule above, whereas unscoped it catches a STRAY COPY that escaped the secret tier, which is the only thing a filename rule adds. That is safe only because 'holdout_answer_key.json' is genuinely distinct from the public dev key's 'dev_answer_key.json' -- NOT a case variant of it. Case cannot distinguish names on a case-insensitive filesystem, so it must never be load-bearing (D38). The invoice-index rule exists for the same reason (D45): the held-out index is agent-denied ground truth under D34, but while it was named 'invoice_index.json' it collided with the three PUBLIC dev indexes and could therefore get no filename rule at all -- protected by directory placement alone, uniquely weaker than every other secret artifact. Generator rules use a '.*' extension wildcard, not '.py', because __pycache__ bytecode is decompilable and so carries the discrepancy-planting rule just as the source does; a stray .pyc would otherwise evade every filename rule. The generator Bash patterns are ANCHORED on a separator or a space rather than bare '*generate.*': unanchored they denied 'bash regenerate.sh', 'npm run pregenerate.build' and even 'git log --grep=generate.py', because the substring appears inside ordinary words -- and 'regenerate' is this project's own workflow verb. Over-blocking is its own failure class (D14): it does not leak, it obstructs, and a guard that obstructs routine work is one people switch off (D65).
